original.title: The theory of planned behavior
original.venue: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes

core_idea: Behaviour is best predicted by the intention to perform it. Intention depends on three things: attitude towards the behaviour, subjective norms (what important others expect), and perceived behavioural control (how easy or hard the person thinks it is). Perceived control can also affect behaviour directly.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: What predicts whether people intend to do something (recycle, use a service, get vaccinated, start a business)?
Which of attitude, norms or perceived control matters most for a given behaviour and group?
Typical data: structured questionnaires built from elicitation interviews, analysed with regression or SEM.
common_mistakes: Writing your own questionnaire items without the elicitation step the theory recommends.
Measuring intention but claiming conclusions about actual behaviour.
Adding extra variables without a reason grounded in the theory or the context.
